commands.review_summary:
Routes failed review-shard recovery through the durable exact-review queue, makes recovery review-only and one-shot, preserves target branches, bounds repository-dispatch retries, and adds focused workflow and queue tests.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: enqueueing a failed-shard recovery while the same item has an ordinary leased entry bypasses the pending-only guard and mutates that active queue entry. A deployed Actions reproduction has not been supplied.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] The contributor needs to fix the repeated active-lease blocker and supply live deployed workflow proof; an automated repair worker cannot provide proof from the GitHub Actions and App installation environment.

target.title: fix(sweep): bound failed shard recovery
target.body:
## Summary

Routes failed review-shard recovery through the durable exact-review queue instead of directly creating a replacement `workflow_dispatch` run.

## Problem

The failed-shard recovery job could repeatedly invoke `sweep.yml` directly for stale open items. That bypassed queue/lease dedupe and produced cancellation/pending churn, including [openclaw/openclaw#67967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67967) and [#92328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92328).

Separately, live target writes obtained an App token but were rejected with `403 Resource not accessible by integration`. A repository PR cannot grant an installed GitHub App additional privileges.

## Implementation

- Replace direct failed-shard `workflow_dispatch` with one `clawsweeper_item` repository-dispatch delivery per item, using the existing durable exact-review queue.
- Preserve the target branch, make recovery review-only, and suppress verdict routing so this recovery path cannot close an item.
- Make recovery one-shot: a failed or expired recovery lease is discarded unless a newer ordinary revision supersedes it; a recovery delivery also cannot overwrite an ordinary pending retry/backoff.
- Retry each repository-dispatch delivery at most three times and report any individual delivery that cannot be queued.
- Add queue and workflow assertions for these invariants.

## Required operational follow-up

Re-authorize the `openclaw-clawsweeper` GitHub App installation for `openclaw/openclaw` with **Issues: Read and write** and **Pull requests: Read and write**. That configuration change is required to restore comment/label/close operations; it is not representable in repository source.

## Validation

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check .github/workflows/sweep.yml dashboard/worker.ts src/repair/publish-event-result.ts test/clawsweeper.test.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts test/sweep-workflow.test.ts`
- `node --test --test-name-pattern='exact event publish and routing require|failed review recovery enters' test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` — 2 passed
- `node --test test/clawsweeper.test.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` — 157 passed
- `pnpm run build:all`

`pnpm run test:unit` was also attempted. Native Windows resolves the hosted Bash-helper tests through Git Bash after its WSL shim is bypassed, but that shell has no `jq`; those hosted-helper checks must remain covered by Linux CI. No portability change is included here. `actionlint` is not installed on this host.

## Codex review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean after the workflow-test update.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.

## Rollout and risk

This changes only recovery scheduling: fresh review requests retain their normal queue/retry behavior. Deploy the workflow after the App installation is re-authorized, then confirm a failed shard creates at most one review-only queued recovery per item and does not revive direct `workflow_dispatch` churn.
